facts.t: India caps the size of its ministry; Britain does not
facts.d: The 91st Amendment fixed the Council of Ministers at 15% of Lok Sabha strength, after ministries had swollen to buy political support. The United Kingdom limits only the number of paid ministers by statute — there is no percentage cap at all.

facts.t: A British minister need not be elected
facts.d: By convention a minister must sit in one of the two Houses — but the Lords will do. A prime minister can appoint an outsider, elevate them to the peerage, and put them in cabinet the same week. India requires membership of either House within six months.

facts.t: Collective responsibility is written down in only one of the two
facts.d: Article 75(3) makes it an express constitutional rule enforceable through a no-confidence motion. In Britain it remains a convention, occasionally suspended outright — as it was for the 1975 and 2016 European referendums.

bank.q: The constitutional cap on the size of the Union Council of Ministers was introduced by:
bank.e: The 91st Amendment fixed it at 15% of Lok Sabha strength. The 52nd Amendment introduced the anti-defection law.

bank.q: Comparing ministers in India and the United Kingdom, consider the following statements:
s: Collective responsibility is an express constitutional rule in India.
In the United Kingdom it is a convention that may be explicitly suspended.
Both systems impose a percentage cap on ministry size.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Only India imposes a percentage cap; British limits are statutory and apply to paid ministers.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a source of ministerial authority in the United Kingdom?
o: A written constitutional article equivalent to Article 74
bank.e: Britain has no codified constitution and therefore no equivalent provision — ministerial office is conventionalised rather than constitutionalised.

bank.q: A person appointed as a minister in India who is not a member of either House must become one within:
bank.e: Six months, failing which they cease to hold office.

bank.as: Anti-defection disqualification bars a person from holding ministerial office in India.
bank.rs: The Tenth Schedule attaches disqualification for the remainder of the term.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Britain has no equivalent — rebellion there is managed politically through the whips rather than legally.

bank.q: Match List I (provision or instrument) with List II (subject):
pairs: 1. Council of Ministers at the state level
2. Prime Minister's duty to furnish information to the President
3. Executive power coextensive with legislative power
4. Duty of British ministers to account to Parliament
bank.e: Article 78 concerns the PM's duty to inform the President, Article 163 the state Council of Ministers, the Ministerial Code British accountability, and Ram Jawaya the scope of executive power.

bank.q: With reference to the head of state, consider the following statements:
s: Under Article 78 the President may require a matter to be placed before the Council of Ministers.
The British monarch has the right to be informed, to be consulted and to warn.
Shamsher Singh held that the President may act independently of ministerial advice.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Shamsher Singh held the opposite — the President and Governors act on aid and advice outside expressly specified discretionary areas.

bank.q: All of the following are categories of Indian ministers EXCEPT:
o: Ministers of State with independent charge
bank.e: Under-Secretaries and Lords Ministers are British categories. India has Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State with and without independent charge, and Deputy Ministers.

bank.q: Ministers in India hold office during the pleasure of:
bank.e: Formally the President, though in practice that reflects the Prime Minister's confidence — the same substance as the British position, differently expressed.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about codes of conduct for ministers:
s: The United Kingdom has a formal Ministerial Code.
India has a single prominent equivalent code.
Indian ministers are bound by oaths, RPA norms and conflict-of-interest rules.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. India has no single consolidated ministerial code — the obligations are scattered across instruments.
